newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan "grieved" by Indian comment on turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan "grieved" by Indian comment on turmoil.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday that remarks by India's foreign minister about a need for New Delhi to watch for political turmoil following prime minister Benazir Bhutto's sacking would not help ties between the arch-rivals.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman said Islamabad was "grieved" by the comments, in which Inder Kumar Gujral said India was keeping a watch on Pakistan in case any rise in political and economic instability spilled over the border.

The New Delhi-based Asian News International (ANI) on Wednesday quoted Gujral as saying Pakistan's political turmoil was an internal matter, "but it would be incorrect for us to assume that whatever changes take place do not affect the neighbouring countries".

The Pakistani spokesman said: "We have the highest regard for the Indian Foreign Minister, but are a little surprised and grieved to see that he has considered it fit to make comments on the internal issues of Pakistan."
"...We feel that the comments of the Indian Foreign Minister on the internal affairs of Pakistan can only be regarded as unhelpful in the area of improvement of our relations."

Pakistan President Farooq Leghari sacked Bhutto and her government earlier this month on disputed charges of corruption and misrule and appointed Meraj Khalid to take over until elections are held on February 3.
Gujral said instability in Pakistan was becoming more highlighted than in the past.
"At the same time, we find the economic situation has a downspin to an extent that they have to import even an expert from the...World Bank to take charge of the ministries."
This was a reference to Shahid Javed Burki, a senior World Bank official who took charge of Pakistan's Finance Ministry after Bhutto was sacked.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars in the nearly five decades thay have been independent from Britain and they have not held official talks for more than two years.
